key_gap: Both sides produced the identical checkable update — prior odds 1:3 (onboarding:speed) × full-data LR e^24 ≈ 3×10^10 → posterior odds ≈ 10^10:1, P(onboarding drives churn) ≈ 1, effect size 30%→10% churn (≈20pp, ~2/3 reduction), policy: kill SLA-as-churn-lever, invest in onboarding completion (>90% within 30 days), re-measure quarterly. The gap is ordering and ownership: the human elicited the org belief as a stated prior with provenance (0.75, anecdote-held) and performed the update as the FIRST move, downgrading the exit-interview channel in one pass ('churn must be measured, not heard') and owning the line 'the measured outcomes did not confirm the anecdotes — they replaced them'; the AI reached the identical structure by first generating and verifying a full alternative set (keep-SLA, split-budget) inside its HOW stage before the update was obvious, stated the said-vs-did insight more cautiously, and only then emitted the posterior arithmetic in its packet.
learning_signal: For org-belief decisions, the update is the entire method and should be the first move: (1) elicit the org's current belief as a stated prior WITH provenance (who holds it, on what channel — anecdote, folklore, or measurement) and treat it as updateable, never as evidence; (2) define the measured outcome by the likelihood it would have under each competing hypothesis BEFORE bringing the data in — a stated prior plus a likelihood is the whole experiment; (3) compute the posterior explicitly (prior odds × likelihood ratio → posterior odds) and check it; (4) license policy by the effect size, not the direction — the 20pp/2/3 reduction, worth ≈0.8pp/mo, is what justifies reallocating the CS budget, and the flat speed cohort is what justifies killing the SLA-as-churn-lever; (5) pre-commit re-measurement (quarterly cohort + segment control) and re-label the anecdote channel from evidence to hypothesis generator — updating is not discarding.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'belief-update first' pre-pass to the WHAT stage for org-policy decisions: (a) WHAT must elicit 'the org's current belief + provenance' as a first-class object before any problem framing; (b) WHY must require the evidence to be stated as likelihoods under competing hypotheses (prior × LR → posterior) before alternatives are generated — for update-shaped problems the alternatives stage should start with the update, not the option set; (c) the decision packet should carry a 'prior → posterior' line with the LR arithmetic, the effect size, and the channel comparison (said vs did) explicitly; (d) re-label anecdotal channels as hypothesis generators in the assumptions line.

key_gap: The pure style executed its core move correctly and then failed on it: it stated the org belief as a prior (0.65, veterans' field observation), defined the measured outcome (cost per ticket by close-out type, 5,000 tickets, Region A pilot at −30%, p<0.001), computed the update (posterior ≈ 0.01), and recommended policy from the posterior (company-wide fast close-outs, cut field time 30%) — and that is where the corruption entered: the likelihood itself was an artifact. Engineers code their own tickets and are paid on closed-ticket count, re-opened jobs were re-logged as NEW tickets with the re-open field never instrumented (rework invisible BY DESIGN), and the Region A dispatcher routed the hard jobs away during the pilot. The measured outcome that 'killed the anecdote' was gamed by the very people being measured, and the anecdote — veterans watching callbacks with their own eyes — was right (informal log: 45% vs 8%). The AI performed the channel audit instead: incentive alignment (self-reported outcome by the compensated party), metric completeness (what is excluded by design), pilot integrity (queue gaming), and gated the update on an independent gaming-resistant re-measurement (third-party 30-day callback audit, random sample, pre-committed reversal thresholds), weighting the prior whose channel was honest and expecting the posterior to reverse to ≈0.98.
learning_signal: Measurement politics — updating on a gamed likelihood with full Bayesian discipline — is the failure mode, not rigor. The core skill is the likelihood-provenance audit, run BEFORE the update: (1) ask who produced the measured outcome and what incentives they faced — a self-reported outcome by the compensated party is a testimony, not a measurement; (2) ask what the metric excludes by design — rework re-logged as new tickets, re-open fields never instrumented: if the quantity the hypothesis predicts (here, callbacks) is unobservable in the data, the likelihood cannot speak to it at all; (3) ask whether the intervention was clean — pilot queue-gaming, cherry-picking, survivorship; (4) weight each channel by its honesty, not its label: a small direct-observation channel (veterans' callback log) can outrank a large gamed metric — 'measured' is not the same as 'honest,' and an anecdotal prior built on direct observation deserves weight, not dismissal; (5) when the likelihood is unverified, the responsible state is NEEDS_EXPERIMENT with a pre-committed, gaming-resistant re-measurement and reversal thresholds — updating garbage likelihoods is disciplined garbage (GIGO).
suggested_improvement: Add a 'likelihood-provenance gate' to the WHY stage for any evidence-driven update: (a) before computing a posterior from supplied data, answer three audit questions — who coded the outcome and under what incentives, what is invisible in the metric by design, and was the intervention clean? — and block the update if any answer is unverifiable; (b) classify evidence channels by honesty (direct observation > independently audited measurement > self-reported/incentive-loaded metrics > stated preference) and weight priors accordingly; (c) when the gating quantity is unmeasured by design, the packet must use the NEEDS_EXPERIMENT state with an independent, gaming-resistant measurement design (third-party coder, random sample, pre-committed reversal thresholds) rather than a computed posterior; (d) add a GIGO check to the packet's evidence line: state what the likelihood cannot see before quoting the posterior.
